drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: A bank's support agent can look up customers and issue refunds. The system prompt says to look up
drills.answer_line: SAM: But this is a bank, and money moves on that call. So, B.
drills.stem: A bank's support agent can look up customers and issue refunds. The system prompt says to look up the customer first, but in about one conversation in 100 it refunds before any lookup. What fixes it?

options.A: Rewrite the instruction in capitals and add three few-shot examples showing the lookup first
options.B: Refund tool rejects calls without a customer ID from a successful lookup, returning an actionable error
options.C: Remove the refund tool and send every refund to a human
options.D: Move to a larger model that follows instructions more reliably

drills.why: Money moves on that call, so the order must hold every time. A improves the odds but cannot guarantee them; order that must hold lives in code.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A healthcare software team of eight wants every developer to use
drills.answer_line: SAM: B. Shared, versioned, no secret in the repo.
drills.scenario: Team-wide MCP server with personal tokens
drills.stem: A team of eight wants every developer to use the same code-hosting MCP server. Each developer has a personal access token. Today only two have it configured. What should the architect do?

options.A: Add the server to the project's .mcp.json with the token committed, so it works on clone
options.B: Add the server to the project's .mcp.json, referencing each token via an environment-variable placeholder
options.C: Ask each developer to add the server at user scope on their own machine
options.D: Describe the server and its setup steps in CLAUDE.md

drills.why: Shared, versioned, no secret in the repo. A leaks a credential, C is eight drifting personal setups, D is guidance about configuration, not configuration.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A utility company's field-service agent calls an M C P tool to book
drills.answer_line: SAM: That is miss pattern two: one correct clause welded to a wrong one. The answer is A
drills.stem: A field-service agent's MCP booking tool returns "request failed" when the scheduler times out, and the agent gives up or keeps retrying a booking the customer's plan does not allow. What is the best change?

options.A: Return errors flagged as errors, with a category, whether to retry, and an actionable explanation
options.B: Have the tool retry silently up to ten times before returning anything
options.C: Add a system-prompt instruction telling the agent never to retry
options.D: Return an empty result on any failure so the agent moves on

drills.why: The agent cannot tell a timeout from a policy refusal unless the error says which. B hides failure and still retries the unretryable one.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A public-sector benefits assistant asks a citizen for their case number
drills.answer_line: ALEX: B. The API is stateless.
drills.stem: A benefits assistant asks for a case number, calls a lookup tool, and three turns later asks again. Logs show each request carries the system prompt and only the latest user message. What is the root cause and fix?

options.A: Context window too small; move to a model with a larger window
options.B: Messages API keeps no memory; resend the full conversation, including tool call and result, every request
options.C: Model ignores earlier turns; add an instruction to remember case numbers
options.D: Raise maximum output tokens so the model can hold more state

drills.why: A standard Messages API call keeps nothing between requests; your code holds the history and sends all of it every turn. A, C and D assume it was ever sent.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A procurement team extracts supplier invoices.
drills.answer_line: SAM: Both. A gives absence a legal value; B gives an unlisted currency one.
drills.stem: Supplier invoice extraction has two failures: a purchase order number appears on invoices that have none, and currencies outside the five listed are reported as the closest listed one. Which two changes address the root causes?

options.A: Make the PO field nullable and instruct the model to return null when absent
options.B: Add an "other" currency enum value with a free-text field for the actual currency
options.C: Make every field required so missing data is caught
options.E: Add a second model pass that rewrites any value it suspects was invented

drills.why: A gives absence a legal value; B gives an unlisted currency one. C is the cause, not the fix. D is scale; E adds a second probabilistic step.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A lender's document pipeline sends all four thousand
drills.answer_line: SAM: Both. They put attention on low confidence and high-risk document types.
drills.stem: A lender's pipeline sends all 4,000 daily extractions to three reviewers, and errors still reach the loan system. Which two changes best focus review where it is needed?

options.A: Route fields whose confidence falls below a threshold calibrated on labelled documents
options.B: Always route document types with a history of low accuracy, such as handwritten income statements
options.C: Add five more reviewers so every extraction is still checked
options.D: Use the model's own stated confidence with a fixed, uncalibrated threshold
options.E: Stop human review entirely and rely on the schema

drills.why: They put attention on low confidence and high-risk document types. C is scale instead of structure, D trusts an unchecked number, E removes a needed gate.

drills.question_line: SAM: Before we wrap, pause and name the six segments from today, each by the symptom that opened it. [pause]
drills.answer_line: ALEX: Unformatted files despite a CLAUDE dot md line.
drills.prompt: Name the six segments from today, each by the symptom that opened it.
drills.answer: Unformatted files despite a CLAUDE.md line; new hire missing the MCP server; wrong tool / no orders when DB down; agent stops half-done; invented policy numbers; three rounds of still wrong.
